content: {"decision":"OPEN","incumbent_segment":"Linear listed-order search of visible receptacles to locate and acquire a target object not initially visible.","evidence_status":{"feasibility_support":"The trajectory successfully acquired tomato_1 after probing fridge_1, countertop_1, then continuing through cabinet_6 down to countertop_2 in listed order.","comparative_support":"No alternative search strategy (e.g., semantic priors for 'tomato' favoring countertops or fridge) was tested; the memory only records this linear approach as feasible, not preferred.","policy_relevance":"A semantically informed search could substantially reduce the 16-step acquisition cost by skipping unlikely receptacles like cabinets for produce."},"functional_contract":{"available_state":"Agent at room center with full list of visible receptacles; target object not yet observed; inventory empty.","local_function":"Systematically navigate to and inspect receptacles in listed order until the target object is found, then take it into inventory.","required_downstream_state":"Target object held in agent inventory; agent located at the receptacle where the target was found.","constraints":["Must eventually find and acquire the target if present in any reachable receptacle","Must not interact with or pick up non-target objects during search","Must open closed receptacles before inspecting their contents"]},"warrant":"The incumbent establishes that strict listed-order search achieves target acquisition, but provides no comparative evidence that this exhaustive traversal is preferable to a semantically guided search. Resolving this comparison could materially reduce search steps in future policy."}
